A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same NC-GCD paper, with all 24 pages and Appendices A-F available. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable matching of equations, figures, tables and appendix content.

before.justification: v2 reports original NC-GCD benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, runtime measurements and feature visualizations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the six-dataset evaluation, appendix backbone comparisons and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The fixed ETF prototypes, supervised and unsupervised alignment losses, Semantic Consistency Matcher and final objective are unchanged. Appendix A's SCM pseudocode and Appendix B.5's category-number estimation procedure are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, ImageNet-100, CUB-200, Stanford Cars, FGVC Aircraft and Herbarium19. The same category-discovery scenarios and appendix evaluations remain; revised dataset citations do not indicate changed coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout corresponding comparisons, including TRAILER and SPT in Table 1 and ProtoGCD and RLCD in Table 8. Bibliographic revisions do not change which methods are evaluated.

E3.justification: The category splits, backbone configurations, training settings, accuracy measures and procedures with given or estimated category counts are unchanged. Appendices A and B retain the same training and sensitivity-experiment protocols.

E4.justification: The alignment and SCM ablations, alpha/beta sensitivity, category-count bias tests, clustering-frequency analysis, efficiency comparisons and visualizations are retained. The new sentence in Section 5.3 points to analyses already present in v2's appendices.

E5.justification: Both retain the fixed-seed category-splitting statement and the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains CUB all-category accuracy of 74.8% with ground-truth K and 70.3% without it; appendix ablation and runtime values also match.

T1.justification: The GCD and Simplex ETF definitions, neural-collapse properties, loss equations and SCM matching formulation are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about consistent ETF alignment, SCM stabilization, category separability and performance across six GCD benchmarks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of alignment, clustering stability, category-count estimation and feature geometry are unchanged. Appendix E retains the limitations concerning untested scalability and sensitivity of clustering-based category-count estimation.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures retain the same projection-head dimensions, optimizer, hyperparameters, training duration, NVIDIA 3090 hardware and SCM pseudocode. No code/data access instructions or other reproducibility information are added or removed.

R1.justification: v3 removes Contrastive representation distillation, cited as reference [39] alongside ImageNet-100 in v2. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged; other reference edits primarily revise bibliographic metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: Section 5.3 gains a short sentence directing readers to existing appendix analyses. Citation numbers, bibliographic author/venue/year/identifier information and the version stamp are edited, while the substantive prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added bold appendix pointer and bibliography edits cause limited text reflow, spacing changes and reference page-break shifts on pages 10-13. Figures, table structures, captions and scientific graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Section 5.3 pointer modestly improves navigation to analyses already available in v2. Reference edits add metadata to some entries while shortening others and removing one citation. These limited editorial gains and losses leave overall quality essentially unchanged, with the scientific evidence, technical documentation and limitations retained.
